summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Optimize quantization profiles. Covered tradeoffs between INT8 and FP8, observed latency/throughput gains, expected quality delta on Nimbus retail workloads, recommended pilot plan and next steps.
transcript:
Header: 2025-11-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Nimbus CTO), Priya Singh (Nimbus ML), Carlos Martinez (Product), Anya Petrova (Infra)

00:00  Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna do a focused walkthrough of Redwood Optimize quantization profiles, specifically INT8 and FP8, call should be about 40 minutes
00:10  Liam O'Connor: great, thanks Maya, quick context - we're evaluating options to reduce per-token cost and meet a 60ms tail latency for our chat summarization path
00:20  Ethan Chen: awesome, that aligns with what we've seen with customers in retail; quick agenda, we'll show console recommendations, dive into quant profiles, share benchmark numbers, then discuss pilot plan
00:40  Priya Singh: just fyi our current stack is hosted LLMs via vendor X and some self-hosted on Kubernetes, main constraints are latency SLO and data residency for PII
01:05  Maya Patel: perfect, and any security gating? SSO, SOC2, KMS?
01:20  Anya Petrova: SOC2 in progress, need audit logs and KMS integration for keys, also VPC peering questions if we move to Dedicated or Private later
01:40  Ethan Chen: noted, Redwood supports KMS and audit logs, can go over docs after. Back to quantization: high level - INT8 is post-training quant that's broadly supported and gives the best cost/throughput wins, FP8 sits between INT8 and FP16 in quality, sometimes slightly better than INT8 on generative quality but requires careful kernel support and tuning
02:15  Carlos Martinez: when you say "best wins" can you quantify? like x latency reduction or x cost reduction?
02:30  Ethan Chen: on typical 13B-style open models we've seen 2.5x-4x throughput improvements vs FP16 depending on batch and sequence length. In latency terms median per-token latency can drop from ~150ms to ~50-70ms in many configs. But numbers depend on prompt length, KV cache hits, and batching.
03:00  Priya Singh: ok that's promising. what's the expected quality delta? we can't tolerate more than 2% quality drop on our summarization metric
03:15  Ethan Chen: good constraint. In our evals across a retail summarization benchmark, INT8 often yields <1.5% drop on ROUGE-like metrics; FP8 usually sits between INT8 and FP16, sometimes matching FP16 on some tasks with small variability. Crucially, Redwood Optimize runs per-customer evals to show the delta on your prompts before recommending a profile
03:45  Liam O'Connor: how reliable are those evals? I mean transcription/metrics sometimes overpromise
03:55  Maya Patel: fair, we run multiple seeds and a holdout set, we also show distributions not just averages. We'll share the raw spreadsheets from previous customers (anonymized) so you can inspect.
04:20  Ethan Chen: a couple of gotchas: INT8 can increase hallucination risk for some tasks if model conditional distributions move, so we recommend a small QA/validation suite. Also INT8 requires care with layer norm and embeddings - Redwood's kernel selector will pick safe execution paths and can fall back to mixed-precision for sensitive layers
04:55  Priya Singh: you mentioned kernel selector - does that mean we need specific instance types or GPUs?
05:10  Ethan Chen: generally no, but FP8 is newer and support varies; Redwood's compilation layer selects kernels based on hardware capabilities. For customers running on H-type GPUs we can prioritize FP8 kernels; for broader hosted fleet we may pick INT8 where FP8 kernels aren't available. We'll show a hardware compatibility table in the follow-up doc
05:40  Carlos Martinez: can we A/B both modes in production? I'd rather do canary then full rollout
05:50  Maya Patel: absolutely - Redwood supports canary rollouts, traffic split, and automatic fallback to FP16 if quality thresholds are breached. That's part of the Optimize playbook we share.
06:15  Liam O'Connor: can you walk through the console now?
06:25  Ethan Chen: sure, switching to shared screen (console demo noises) - landing page shows recommended profiles. For Nimbus we ran a quick auto-profile with a small sample and it suggested INT8-agg and FP8-safe as candidate profiles. The recommendations include expected latency, token cost, and predicted quality delta
07:00  Priya Singh: the "INT8-agg" name, what does that encode?
07:05  Ethan Chen: naming scheme: precision-target_workload-e.g., INT8-chat or INT8-agg for aggregated workloads. It also tags profiles with recommended batching and KV cache settings. You can preview per-route expected token cost changes and a per-prompt quality delta distribution
07:30  Maya Patel: note, these deltas are conservative; we bias toward safety when recommending production profiles. For experiments you can pick more aggressive profiles.
07:45  Anonymous Speaker 1: (unintelligible)
08:00  Ethan Chen: back to numbers, here's an example from a 13B convo bot: FP16 baseline median latency 140ms, INT8 profile 62ms, FP8 profile 78ms; quality measured on the summarization task: FP16 baseline 0.0% delta, FP8 +0.4% variance, INT8 -1.1% delta on our metric. Those are illustrative but inline with what we've seen
08:35  Priya Singh: acceptable. Does Redwood provide automatic rollback if quality drops in production?
08:45  Maya Patel: yes. You can configure metric monitors and automatic rollback thresholds, or have canaries with manual checkpoints.
09:00  Liam O'Connor: about batching - our clients are latency sensitive, we can't accept big batching delays to achieve throughput
09:10  Ethan Chen: understood. Redwood Optimize suggests small batches and micro-batching, and will optimize for latency SLOs; you can set the policy to prioritize tail latency over cost and it'll tune batching and pre-warming accordingly
09:30  Carlos Martinez: what about caching? for our summarization path we often hit prefix reuse
09:40  Ethan Chen: great fit - Redwood supports prefix and KV caching which multiplies effective throughput for repeated prompts and long contexts. Combine caching + INT8 for biggest wins. For example, cache hit scenarios show >4x effective throughput vs cold runs
10:05  Priya Singh: any examples of where FP8 beats INT8 in quality?
10:15  Ethan Chen: FP8 sometimes preserves dynamic range on outlier activations better, so on tasks with rare tokens or long-range math-ish conditioning FP8 can reduce drop compared to INT8. But FP8's improvements aren't universal; that's why per-customer evals are key
10:40  Maya Patel: also note operationally FP8 can be trickier on some infra, so there's a trade: slightly better quality vs narrower hardware support and more tuning.
11:00  Liam O'Connor: curious about cost models - how do we price dedicated kernels or FP8 usage?
11:10  Maya Patel: for hosted API it's usage-based pricing with distinct effective token costs per profile; for Dedicated we can provide reserved capacity pricing and factor in expected throughput improvements. We'll include differential pricing examples in the deck
11:30  Priya Singh: security question: if we run a Dedicated cluster with FP8 kernels, does Redwood handle KMS and audit or do we need to manage keys?
11:45  Ethan Chen: Redwood can integrate with your KMS and maintain audit logs; for Private deployments keys can stay in your HSM. We'll include the security doc link after the call
12:10  Carlos Martinez: what does the pilot look like practically? 2-4 week POC?
12:20  Maya Patel: typical pilot is 2-3 weeks: you provide sample prompts and SLOs, we run offline evals and a small in-prod canary, then review results and choose a profile for rollout. If you want a longer reliability run we can extend it
12:40  Priya Singh: timeline-wise we want results before Black Friday testing window, so tighter scheduling would help
12:50  Maya Patel: noted, we can prioritize Nimbus, recommend starting the sample prompt send this week and we can begin baseline runs early next week
13:05  Ethan Chen: I'll own the benchmark run. Quick note on methodology: we'll run FP16 baseline, then FP8 and INT8 variants across your prompt set at multiple batch sizes, measure median/95/99 latencies and quality deltas; we'll also surface token cost and memory headroom
13:40  Liam O'Connor: what about tooling to replay traffic?
13:50  Ethan Chen: Redwood has a small replay harness we can provide that accepts exported request traces and replays them against candidate profiles in a staging environment
14:10  Priya Singh: can we tie the evaluation to our internal metrics, not only ROUGE? we have a custom relevancy score
14:20  Ethan Chen: yes, bring the metric, we'll compute it as long as it's deterministic on outputs; if it's human-eval heavy we'll do sample human grading or automated proxies
14:40  Maya Patel: any other major blockers from your side?
14:45  Priya Singh: just scheduling and getting the prompt set, and ensuring data redaction before sending
15:00  Carlos Martinez: fine from product side
15:05  Anya Petrova: infra notes - need to know required instance sizes for dedicated pilot and network egress implications
15:20  Ethan Chen: we'll include an infra sizing recommendation based on your throughput targets; generally INT8 reduces GPU memory and can run on smaller instance types vs FP16
15:45  Maya Patel: ok quick recap of action items and next steps
15:50  Maya Patel: Ethan will run the benchmark and share spreadsheet; I'll send pricing and the Optimize playbook with rollout templates; Priya to share 1k prompts and SLOs; we'll aim for initial runs next week
16:10  Liam O'Connor: thanks team, useful session, let's sync on 11/24 for the deep benchmark review
16:20  Maya Patel: great, we'll follow up with calendar invite and links
16:30  (call ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-attributions and filler; references to kernel names and GPUs generalized. Shared artifacts: link: /redwood/optimize/playbook (provided), link: /redwood/benchmarks/nimbus-sample-template.csv (placeholder)
